title: Childrens Support Worker
description:
Key Care & Support are looking for experienced Children's Support workers

Various shifts available.

We do not offer sponsorships

You will need to be

A driver - with a UK Drivers Licence ( minimum of 12 months in the UK )

Fully flexible regarding your availability with a minimum of 30 hours availability every week

Have excellent communication skills- both verbal and written

Person centred and committed to delivering the highest standard of care and support

Full and part time contracts available

In return we can offer

Guaranteed hours

Continuity of support to people we care for

Competitive rates of pay

Pension contributions

Training and professional development

Join the team and be part of an organisation passionate about contributing to make the best for people with a learning disability and autism to live a quality of life they desire.

We have work opportunities in and around Trafford. These roles are ongoing and regular hours - not 20 minute call- ins. You will be based in one location.

Weekend Support is essential for this role

What you will do

As a Childrens Support Worker you will be expected to provide an outstanding level of support that will help to ensure the people we support live a more comfortable, dignified, liberated and happy life. You will have excellent communication skills and be a naturally caring and patient personality.

Typical responsibilities may include:
- Supporting children in the family home
- Excellent communication skills and relationship building supporting the people we support to understand the world around them and promoting positive relationships.
- Community and social Inclusion supporting children to access and participate in their local community and social events to promote life skills and individuality.
- Personal care helping people to get ready for the day. This may include prompting the people we support to take their medication and assisting with bathing, showering and using the bathroom. Not all Support Worker roles include high levels of personal care.

What you will bring to your role

Duties will vary depending on the personal needs of each person however, as a Children's Support Worker you should have:
- energy and enthusiasm to provide an outstanding level of support including travelling and taking part in activities in the community.
- excellent communication skills which help people understand the world around them and prompts positive relationships.
- a naturally caring and patient personality ensuring the people you support feel liberated, happy, and are treated fairly, with respect and dignity. Responsibilities may include helping people use the bathroom take medication and assist with bathing, although not all Support Worker roles involve personal care duties.
- great organisation skills to keep accurate records, carrying out all recording and reporting in a person-centred, factual manner. Y
- the ability to work safely and ensure contractual and regulatory compliance so our clients and their family can trust, feel safe and have confidence in the support we provide.

In addition, as the role of a Children's Support Worker can be challenging at times, it is essential to have a positive mind-set with a desire to improve the lives of those with a learning disability. You will need to be quick thinking with a positive can-do attitude.

At Key Care & Support, we value a diverse and inclusive workplace and we intentionally plan for the success of our colleagues in everything we do.

We are proud to be a Disability Confident Leader and welcome applicants with disabilities to apply for all roles with us.

All roles are subject to an enhanced DBS check and suitable references.

More information about the role

We work in partnership with people with a learning disability and/or autism. We do this by providing high quality, flexible services that support people, including young adults and children, to live as independently as possible in their own homes and in the community.

Everyone wants a purposeful job - to do something meaningful, we can give you that. You will have opportunities to develop as a person, colleague, leader and advocate.

You ll make new friends and feel inspired to reach your potential. We will ask a lot of you - but you ll get back so much more. With us, it is never just a job .

In return for your hard work and passion, we can give you real meaning and purpose in your work.

What Key Care & Support will give you

As well as knowing that what we do is making a positive difference to people s lives, you will receive fair pay and have access to a wide range of rewards and benefits as one of our employees.
- Real living wage
- 5.6 days holiday inc of bank holidays.
- Pension contributions into NEST Scheme on a salary sacrifice basis meaning NI savings.
- Free access to round the clock employee assistance program for advice and support.
- Quarterly award scheme and recognition at every 5 years through our long service award program.
- Access to training and professional development opportunities.
- Long service awards.
- Recognition awards for excellence in service delivery.
- Birthday care and gift card

title: Residential Childcare Worker
description:
Residential Childcare Worker
Children's Residential - Stalybridge SK15
Job Role
A rewarding opportunity to make a genuine difference in the lives of children and young people.
A children's residential home in Stalybridge is looking to recruit caring, reliable and dedicated individuals to help create a safe, supportive and welcoming environment for young people.
Previous experience in residential childcare isn't essential. What's most important is having the right values, emotional resilience and a genuine passion for supporting young people. Full training and development opportunities will be provided.
Responsibilities
You'll be part of a close-knit team helping children feel safe, supported and optimistic about their future. Your responsibilities will include:
Building positive relationships based on trust, consistency and respect.
Supporting daily routines, including school runs, meals, activities and emotional support.
Providing reassurance and being a reliable adult during challenging moments.
Maintaining accurate records of key events and each child's progress.
Promoting education, wellbeing, independence, life skills and positive experiences.
Helping to create a warm, welcoming environment where children feel at home.
Requirements
This opportunity could suit someone who:
Has experience in care, education, youth work or a similar setting, although this isn't essential.
Has strong interpersonal skills, emotional resilience and a natural ability to build relationships.
Can remain calm and consistent during challenging situations.
Is willing to learn about supporting children who have experienced trauma and adversity.
Is comfortable working independently when required and following structured routines.
Holds a full UK driving licence and has access to a car (essential).
A Level 3 qualification in Residential Childcare or Level 4 qualification in Children, Young People and Families is desirable but not essential. Those without the relevant qualification will be supported through a fully funded Level 4 Children, Young People and Families Practitioner qualification.
Salary, Benefits & Development
13.50 per hour.
1,000 welcome bonus ( 500 upon successful completion of induction and 500 upon successful completion of probation).
2 days on, 4 days off rota, averaging approximately 10 working days per month.
Paid overtime at 14.50 per hour.
Sleep-ins available as required, paid at 75 per night.
Fully funded Level 4 qualification.
Structured induction, ongoing training, regular supervision and coaching.
Opportunities for career progression and further development.
Cash health plan, employee recognition awards, crisis fund and long-service recognition.
Two additional days of annual leave each year, increasing to three after your first year and four after your second year.
Rota pattern designed to support a healthy work-life balance.
Additional Information
The 1,000 welcome bonus is subject to repayment on a pro-rata basis if an employee voluntarily leaves or is dismissed for misconduct within their first 12 months.
All successful applicants will be subject to safer recruitment and pre-employment checks. A charge of up to 74.70 may initially apply for right-to-work checks, ID checks and DBS applications, where applicable. These costs are refundable following successful completion of induction.

Search is an equal opportunities recruiter and we welcome applications from all suitably skilled or qualified applicants, regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/beliefs, sexual orientation or age.

title: Family Support Worker
description:
Prospectus is delighted to be supporting our client in their search for a Family Support Worker to join their specialist Missing Service in Manchester. This is a rewarding opportunity for an experienced family support professional to work alongside parents, carers and families affected by complex safeguarding concerns, helping them build resilience, strengthen relationships and improve outcomes for children and young people. This is a fixed term contract until March 2027, with the potential to be extended and if offering £26,100 per annum. This position will require travel across Greater Manchester, and surrounding areas (travel is expensed). For this role, we can also consider flexible working arrangements, such as part-time hours, term-time only arrangements or compressed hours, for the right candidate.

The successful candidate will bring demonstrable experience of working directly with parents, carers, children and young people, ideally within a family support, early help, youth work, safeguarding or whole-family setting. Whilst experience supporting parents of children who go missing from home would be highly advantageous, the organisation's priority is finding someone with a proven ability to engage and support parents and carers facing challenging circumstances and who understands the complexities that can place young people at risk.

You will work closely with parents and carers of children who have experienced, or are at risk of, missing episodes, providing practical guidance, emotional support and advocacy. The role focuses on helping parents and carers better understand risk, strengthen communication and develop strategies that improve safety and reduce vulnerability.

To be successful, you will have:
- Significant experience working with parents, carers and families, ideally within a whole-family or family-centred support environment.
- A strong understanding of child exploitation, including criminal exploitation, sexual exploitation, county lines, online exploitation and contextual safeguarding.
- Sound knowledge of risk indicators, online safety concerns and the impact exploitation can have on children, young people and wider family networks.
- Experience supporting families affected by complex and sensitive issues, using a trauma-informed and non-judgemental approach.
- Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to build trust with parents and carers.
- Experience working collaboratively with statutory and voluntary sector partners, including social care, education, health and police services.
- Excellent safeguarding knowledge and an understanding of current legislation and best practice relating to vulnerable children and young people.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to advocate effectively on behalf of families.

Additional requirements:
- Full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle for work purposes.
- An active Enhanced DBS would be highly advantageous, although candidates willing to undertake the appropriate checks will also be considered.
- Flexibility to occasionally work outside standard office hours where required.

At Prospectus, we invest in your journey as a candidate and are committed to supporting you with your application. We welcome candidates from a diverse range of backgrounds and are happy to make reasonable adjustments to enable all interested candidates to apply. If you require assistance with your application, please contact Shannon Sanderson, the lead consultant for this role. Please note that applications and CVs sent directly by email cannot be accepted and must be submitted through the application link to ensure they are properly recorded and considered.

title: Behaviour Support Assistant
description:
Learning Support Assistant - SEMH (Secondary SEND School)
Stockport
450 - 550 per week
Full-time Term-time only Long-term role with permanent opportunities

Flexible and quick-thinking in a dynamic school environment
A strong team player with a proactive approach
Ideal experience:
Residential care / children's homes
Foster care or family support
Youth work, mentoring, or coaching
Sports, behaviour support, or alternative provision settings

450- 550 per week (depending on experience)

A fantastic school environment with excellent resources and support

Apply today to be considered for this role.

title: Care Assistant - Care Home
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Care Assistant at Barchester, you'll play a vital role in helping our residents enjoy each day to the fullest. Providing both practical support and meaningful companionship, you'll make a genuine difference to the lives of the people you care for.

In this role, you'll:
- Support residents with daily living activities and personal care
- Help residents with food and drink throughout the day
- Build positive relationships and provide companionship
- Follow individual care plans and support resident wellbeing
- Spend valuable one-to-one time with residents
- Encourage independence while promoting dignity and respect
- Work as part of a caring team to deliver high-quality support

No two days are ever the same, making this a rewarding opportunity to use your skills, develop your experience and make a real impact every day.

ABOUT YOU

We're looking for someone who is kind, compassionate and committed to delivering excellent care.

To join us as a Care Assistant, you'll have:
- Experience caring for older people
- A positive, can-do attitude
- Excellent communication and people skills
- A warm, empathetic and respectful approach
- A genuine passion for supporting others

Above all, you'll have the compassion and dedication needed to provide the highest standard of care and support. In return, we'll give you all the training and development you need to succeed.

REWARDS PACKAGE

In return for your dedication, you'll receive a competitive rate of pay plus a sector-leading benefits and rewards package, including:
- Free training and development opportunities
- Access to wellbeing and support tools
- A range of retail discounts and savings
- Unlimited referrals through our Refer a Friend bonus scheme
- Employee of the Month recognition
- Long Service Awards
- Career development opportunities within one of the UK's leading care providers

And so much more!

If you'd like to use your people skills in an organisation that provides the quality of care you'd expect for your own loved ones, this is a rewarding place to be.

Our Care Home Manager is always happy to welcome you into the home for an informal chat, so feel free to pop in and find out more about working at Barchester.

title: Behaviour Support Assistant
description:
Are you a compassionate and dedicated professional with experience in supporting students with challenging behaviour? Do you have a background in working with SEND and a strong understanding of managing complex behaviours? If so, we want to hear from you!

- Implement effective strategies to manage and de-escalate challenging behaviour.
- Work closely with the class teacher and other professionals to create an individualised support plan.
- Assist with academic work where necessary, ensuring the pupil remains engaged and supported.
- Foster a positive, safe, and inclusive learning environment.
- Record and report on pupil progress, behaviours, and interventions.

The Ideal Candidate:
- Previous experience working with SEND or with students who exhibit challenging behaviour.
